elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: The proviso permits either party, including Customer, to assign to an affiliate on written notice and without consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in connection with a merger.
elements.evidence: The proviso expressly permits assignment without consent to a successor in connection with a merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in connection with an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The proviso expressly permits assignment without consent to a successor in connection with an acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without Vendor consent to a successor in connection with a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The proviso permits assignment without consent to a successor in connection with a sale of all or substantially all assets.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign the Agreement without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: The mutual proviso allows Vendor to assign without Customer consent to an affiliate or to a successor in the listed transactions.

elements.element: Customer consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: For assignments subject to consent, the opening language states that consent will not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign the Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no competitor prohibition and could permit a consent-free assignment to a competitor that is Vendor's affiliate or transactional successor.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate the Agreement because of Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause grants no termination right arising from Customer's change of control.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The proviso permits either party to assign without consent to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganisation, or sale of all or substantially all assets.

elements.element: Customer must provide written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The successor-assignment carve-out is expressly conditioned on written notice.

elements.element: Vendor may assign the Agreement to a successor without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: The mutual proviso permits Vendor to assign without consent to a successor in connection with the listed transactions.

elements.element: Vendor must provide written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The successor-assignment carve-out applies to either party and is conditioned on written notice.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than assignments to successors require Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Customer may also assign to an affiliate without Vendor consent, even where the affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Vendor consent to other Customer assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: For Customer assignments that remain subject to consent, the clause provides that consent will not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor assignments other than assignments to successors require Customer consent.
elements.evidence: Vendor may also assign to an affiliate without Customer consent, even where the affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Customer consent to other Vendor assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: For Vendor assignments that remain subject to consent, the clause provides that consent will not be unreasonably withheld.

result.reason: The operative language gives Customer the preferred affiliate and transactional-successor rights, but improperly gives the same consent-free rights to Vendor and contains no competitor restriction. It also misses the fallback because affiliate assignments are exempted from consent even though the fallback exempts only successor assignments. The proviso is otherwise clear and does not create an internal contradiction, but its mutual affiliate carve-out is broader than necessary for either complete position.
